input.quote: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
input.rationale: Article IV (p0049) gives the Licensor a unilateral option to extend the 36-month Initial Period by a further seven years, with no Licensee opt-out and no cap on renewal pricing. That is a multi-year renewal imposed at the Vendor's election, which sits in walk-away territory and fails both the preferred position (mutual renewal, or 12-month auto-renewal with a 30-day opt-out and CPI/3% uplift cap) and the fallback (auto-renewal with a notice window of no more than 60 days and uplift ≤5%). The mutual-extension language in Article IV(II)-(III) is inconsistent with the Licensor option sentence and does not cure it. We therefore replaced the seven-year Licensor-option renewal with successive 12-month renewals, a 30-day non-renewal notice right for either party, and an uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

proposal.summary: Replace Licensor-option seven-year renewal with 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out and capped uplift
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a seven-year extension exercisable at the Licensor's sole option; our playbook allows renewal only by mutual agreement or automatic twelve-month terms we can exit on 30 days' notice, with uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. We have conformed the renewal mechanic accordingly, consistent with the mutual-extension language already in Article IV(II)-(III).

ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
ops.newText: The Agreement may be renewed for successive additional periods of twelve (12) months each, provided that either party may elect not to renew by giving written notice not less than thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current period, and any increase in fees for any renewal period shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in CPI over the preceding period and three percent (3%).
